summary: Turn 10. The map clarification was accepted (audit_spec_version is now 2). This turn resolves the active Candidate 0069a1fe5be04660b3b91f31ac2394d4 as explained by an existing mechanism, not escalated. The gap is real and now recorded in the map: a higher-ballot AcceptReply is dropped at the equality gate (epaxos/epaxos.go:1024-1026), so handleAcceptReply never counts a nack or calls makeBallot/bcastPrepare. But non-completion at that ballot is not final for the instance: every replica's executeCommands re-examines each row and, when the head instance stays non-executable for COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, enqueues instancesToRecover (epaxos/epaxos.go:385-435); startRecoveryForInstance rebuilds the bookkeeping and calls makeBallot then bcastPrepare (epaxos/epaxos.go:1127-1169). makeBallot uses r.Id for the row owner and r.Id+N for a non-owner, with an IsLeader jumping past maxRecvBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451), so an equal-or-higher recovery ballot is available without the Accept-path escalation; acceptors adopt it in handlePrepare (epaxos/epaxos.go:1183-1187) and handlePrepareReply re-enters Accept or phase 1 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1314). The missing nack therefore costs at most the timer interval plus a recovery round rather than permanent stalling. Submitted action=explained with the question (disposition explained_by_existing_mechanism, activity_classes A1/A2, obligation_relation_kind recovery, principal fact F-DECISION, direct behavior B-ACCEPT-REPLY-LEADER, supporting B-EXEC / B-RECOVERY-START / B-PREPARE-REPLY-LEADER / B-PREACCEPT-REPLY-LEADER). Counterevidence keeps the protection honestly attributed to the independent recovery timer (makeBallot does not always raise the ballot, so a single recovery can fail against a higher stored ballot), and remaining keeps the latency/ballot-range question, the missing explicit progress-duty grounding, the unchecked A1 fast path, and unread A4 membership and A6 durability.
